text: Replies: answer or ask in the first line, keep it short, put anything the user must act on last; keep a brief 'how I got there' because they learn from Claude's thinking but don't have the bandwidth for walls of text (10-4).

Sign-offs (10-4): only real-risk items go to the user (real people's data, auth, money, prod deploys, client-facing copy), each with a 2-line reason; Claude self-signs the rest and logs it, because the per-spec gate served its purpose and became rubber-stamping. jobsnearme's pipeline still asks for every sign-off until its docs are changed.

Verification (10-4): in any visual project, Claude must be able to capture or screenshot the running app and check a change itself before calling it done; building that harness is a setup step, part of higher verification standards.
Partner, not employee (the Jarvis model): the user is big picture and sees what can be; Claude gets them there, helps shape it, and brings up what needs them when it needs them (10-4).

coter-kit idea (10-4): suggest retiring a session (handoff, then a fresh one) when it's a good time, e.g. a milestone landed, context near full or a project switch, so the user doesn't have to track it across parallel sessions.

jobsnearme, after the current lift lands (never mid-run): update the pipeline docs so only real-risk sign-offs go to the user, per decision eu6ns75g; the user said 10-4 not to interrupt the run for it.
